decision: Did not re-close the ticket. The agency closed it "completed without payment" on the landlord's "all done" (event-034, event-036, event-037), but the landlord's next message the same day asks whether a new appointment date has been arranged with the tenants (event-038), so completion is not verifiable and CAP-CLOSE's final checks are not met. No contractor instructed and no spend: the landlord used his own window firm (event-011, event-017), so CAP-DISPATCH-ROUTINE / APR-SPEND-OVER-CAP never engaged. I asked the landlord to confirm finished-or-further-visit (ACT-2), asked the tenant to confirm the state of the windows and offered to book access with 24 hours' notice (ACT-3, CAP-SCHEDULE-ACCESS), logged the status and address conflicts (ACT-1), referred the address data conflict to the office rather than asserting an address to any party (ACT-4, rule 2 / ESC-CONFLICT), and put the job on hold Waiting for Landlord (ACT-5). Routine, non-emergency: blown/failed glazing is not an emergency definition and no hazard keyword appears in the artefacts.
recap: Glazing job closed on the landlord's "all done" but he then asked about a new appointment; reopened, asked landlord and tenant to confirm, address conflict sent to the office.
hold_reason: Waiting for Landlord — confirmation whether his own contractor has finished the kitchen window and patio door glazing or a further visit is due; 3 working days from 2025-04-04, then office to phone.
next_step: Landlord to confirm whether the glazing work is complete or a further appointment is needed (asked ACT-2, 3 working day clock); tenant's answer on the state of the windows (ACT-3) corroborates.

facts.statement: Tenant reported kitchen window and patio door windows on 2025-01-14; the agency later characterised the fault as the windows being "blown" (failed double glazing) and the tenant supplied photographs but little description.
The agency's own system required landlord approval before any instruction on this job ("Please complete landlord approval step first").
The tenant confirmed the request did not originate from the landlord.

The landlord elected to use his own contractors: an email relayed on 24 January instructs his contractor to quote for replacing the windows only, stating budget exists for the windows but not the patio door glass, which was to be quoted "for the future".
The tenant gave authorisation on 30 January for her contact details to be passed to the landlord's surveyor.

On 2025-02-15 the landlord said he had received a quote and asked his contractor to proceed; the agency kept the job open pending completion. The quote amount, VAT and provider were never recorded on the ticket.

Between 1 March and 29 March the job sat on hold awaiting the landlord's window company to arrange a visit; a hold note of 29 March records "Visitng on Tuesday 6th June", a date inconsistent with the agency's 4 April question about "the visit on Monday".
On 2025-04-04 11:08 the landlord replied "Good, all done!"; the agency recorded "LL completed by himself" and "Task has been completed without payment".
At 2025-04-04 12:05 the landlord asked whether a new appointment date has been arranged with the tenants, 57 minutes after confirming the job was done.
No agency contractor was ever instructed and no agency spend arose on this job; all work was arranged directly by the landlord.
The ticket names six different property addresses across its events; only the case record and event-032 use Flat 26, 116 Copperfield Walk, Alderwick, ZZ7 8ZZ.

Nothing in the artefacts matches an emergency definition: no gas, electrical, water ingress, heating loss, insecurity or loss of water is reported; the glazing units are described as blown, not broken open.

conflicts.description: The landlord confirms the work is complete and then asks about arranging a new appointment with the tenants, 57 minutes apart.
conflicts.resolution: Asked the landlord to confirm which is correct (ACT-2, 3 working day clock) and asked the tenant to report the state of the windows (ACT-3). Ticket held open rather than re-closed.

conflicts.description: Agency records disagree on the property: case record Flat 26, 116 Copperfield Walk, Alderwick vs Flat 12, 182 Meadow Row, Kingshaven on every outbound template, plus four further addresses in landlord and contractor messages.
conflicts.resolution: Not decided by me. Conflict logged (ACT-1) and referred to the office (ACT-4). Tenant correspondence used the case-record address only; no address asserted to the landlord.

conflicts.description: Hold note of 29 March records a visit "Tuesday 6th June" while the agency asked on 4 April how "the visit on Monday" went.
conflicts.resolution: Immaterial to the next step; noted as data quality. Completion is being confirmed with the landlord and tenant directly.

red_flags.description: Six different property addresses appear across one ticket, including in outbound agency emails to the tenant and landlord. Any one of them could have sent a contractor or a letter to the wrong flat.
red_flags.action_taken: Logged (ACT-1) and referred to the property manager queue (ACT-4); used only the case-record address with the tenant and no address with the landlord.

red_flags.description: Two landlord emails are written in the third person about the landlord himself ("Theo has arranged...", "Theo is inquiring..."), suggesting a relayed or machine-summarised message rather than the landlord's own words; both carry addresses that match no other record.
red_flags.action_taken: Treated as evidence only and put the question back to the landlord in his own channel for confirmation (ACT-2) rather than acting on the content.

red_flags.description: Job was marked complete and "completed without payment" on a four-word landlord email with no provider report, photos or tenant confirmation, then contradicted within the hour.
red_flags.action_taken: Declined to re-close; held open pending landlord and tenant confirmation (ACT-5).
